lines.en: Hey Ben! **Are you free on** Saturday?
lines.pt: Oi, Ben! Você está livre no sábado?

lines.en: **Let’s** go to the new food market. **How about** two o’clock?
lines.pt: Vamos ao novo mercado de comida. Que tal às duas?

lines.en: I work until one. Is three o’clock okay?
lines.pt: Eu trabalho até uma. Pode ser às três?

lines.en: Three is fine. Where do we meet?
lines.pt: Às três está bom. Onde nos encontramos?

lines.en: **How about** the park gate? It’s close to the market.
lines.pt: Que tal no portão do parque? É perto do mercado.

lines.en: **Sounds good!** **Let’s** grab a coffee after, too.
lines.pt: Boa! Vamos tomar um café depois também.

lines.en: Great idea! I’ll text you on Saturday morning.
lines.pt: Ótima ideia! Mando uma mensagem no sábado de manhã.

lines.en: Perfect. **Sounds good!** See you at three.
lines.pt: Perfeito. Combinado! A gente se vê às três.

pages.title: Making plans

situation.text: You want to do something fun with a friend this weekend. You find out if the friend is free, suggest an activity, agree on a time and a place.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can invite someone, suggest a time and a place, accept or change a plan and confirm it.
canDo: Ask if someone is free: Are you free on…?
Suggest a time or place: How about…?
Accept or change a plan: Sounds good! / Is… okay?
success: I ask if my friend is free.
I agree on time and place.
pages.think: When you make plans with friends in Brazil, do you decide the time and place in the first message? What do you write?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação: combinar um passeio no fim de semana.
solo: Pergunte em português: “Como você combina um programa com um amigo?”.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso.
group: Cada estudante diz uma atividade de fim de semana (movie, park, coffee…).
Mostre a cena e pergunte: What day is it? Where are they?
extra: What do you do on Saturdays?
Who do you make plans with?
support: Aceite palavras soltas: Saturday, park, coffee, three.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.group: Each student asks a neighbor about the weekend.

pages.recall: Asking for directions: “Where is…? / Turn left”. Ask: Where is your favorite place in the city? How do you get there?

extra: What did you do last weekend?
Do you prefer going out or staying home?

errors.w: I go to the cinema in the weekend.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Making plans in the USA
pages.intro: Friends in the USA often make plans by text, with a day, a time and a place. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: Many friends make plans by text: “Free Saturday?” and then they choose the time and the place.
A casual, friendly invitation. It can be vague, so people often add a day and a time.
For appointments and work, being on time matters. With friends, a few minutes late is usually fine, but send a text.

qs.q: How do friends often make plans?

levels.A2: They usually text and agree on a day, a time and a place.
levels.B1: Most people text first, then decide the day, the time and where to meet.
levels.B2: Plans are often made informally by text, then confirmed with a final message closer to the time.

qs.q: What does “Let’s grab a coffee” mean?
qs.pt: O que significa “Let’s grab a coffee”?

levels.A2: It is a friendly invitation to have a coffee together.
levels.B1: It is a casual way to invite someone for a coffee and a chat.
levels.B2: It is a relaxed invitation, sometimes without a fixed time, so a concrete suggestion makes it a real plan.

qs.q: What do you do if you are late?
qs.pt: O que fazer se você vai se atrasar?

levels.B1: Send a quick message such as “I’m running about ten minutes late.”
levels.B2: Let the other person know as soon as you can and say roughly how late you will be.

pages.compare: In Brazil, being a little late to a social event is often normal, and people sometimes say “chego já”. In the USA, it is polite to arrive near the agreed time or to text if you are late. Does it change with the event where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural: combinar por mensagem, convite casual e pontualidade.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare o “chego já” com avisar o atraso por mensagem.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Are you usually on time?”.
answers: Q1: by text; day, time, place.
Q2: casual invitation to have coffee.
extra: Are you usually on time?
Do you prefer texting or calling?
support: Use as respostas A1 como modelo.
stretch: B2: discuta quando um convite vago é só educação e quando é um plano real.

teach.goal: Entender dia, hora e lugar antes de ver o texto.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: o que combinam. 2ª escuta: dia, horas, lugar e o plano extra.
Peça que preencha uma agenda no papel.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas preenchem a agenda.
Compare as agendas.
answers: Pass 1: making plans for the weekend.
Pass 2: Saturday · two o’clock · three · park gate · coffee.
extra: Why does Ben change the time?
Who will send a text?

qs.q: Why does Ben say three o’clock?
What does Maya suggest after the market?

group: Leitura em duplas; troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia.
answers: He works until one · at the park gate · Saturday · grab a coffee
extra: What would you suggest instead of the market?
How do you say no politely?

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Check if the friend is available.
Suggest a time or a place.

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again today: Are you free on…? · Let’s… · How about…? · Sounds good!

teach.goal: Escolher 4 chunks e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de traduzir.
Peça um convite real para o próximo fim de semana.
group: Cada estudante convida o colega ao lado.
Duplas: aceitem ou recusem com educação.
answers: Checking · Suggesting activity · Suggesting time/place · Accepting · Saying no
extra: Which one do you use with friends only?
How do you say no politely?
support: Use só Are you free…? e Sounds good! na primeira rodada.

patterns.name: Asking about availability
ex: Are you free on Friday night?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Would you like to have a coffee with me?
Unfortunately, I am not available on Friday.
register.note: Text messages are shorter and use contractions: “Free Sat?” In a formal email, use full sentences.

teach.goal: Fixar “Let’s…” e “How about…?”; “Are you free on…?” como abertura.
solo: Mostre os padrões DENTRO do diálogo.
Troque as peças e peça a frase completa (agora são 3 peças).
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça.
Pares: A convida, B aceita ou propõe outro horário.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão.
extra: Say yes. Say no. Suggest another time.
Plan a trip with three suggestions.

errors.w: How about we go to the market? (confuso com Let’s)
errors.r: How about going to the market? / Let’s go to the market.

support: Fique só com “Let’s + verbo” na primeira rodada.
stretch: Responda a um convite recusando e propondo outro dia.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In plans, the important words are stressed: days, times, places. “Are you FREE on SATurday?” The small words (are, you, on) are weak.

own.prompt: Write one invitation with a day and a time. Underline the strong words.
own.criteria: Say it twice: first every word strong, then only days and times strong. Which sounds more natural?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: ênfase nas palavras importantes (dia, hora, lugar).
solo: Bata palmas só nas palavras fortes.
Peça que o estudante diga o convite próprio com ênfase.
group: Coro; depois duplas.
Cada estudante diz o próprio convite.
answers: Identify 1: Are you free on Saturday? · Identify 2: How about two o’clock?

errors.w: ARE YOU FREE ON SATURDAY (tudo forte)

support: Reduza a velocidade e bata palmas.

items.text: ___ go to the park on Sunday!

items.q: You are busy at 7. Choose the best reply.
opts: Sorry, I’m busy at seven. How about eight?
items.why: Refuse politely and suggest another time.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça uma recusa educada.
group: Duplas; comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: Let’s see a movie! · 2: How about seven o’clock? · 3: Are you free on Friday? · 4: Sounds good!
Gap: Let’s · on · How about four o’clock? · Sounds good! · Yes, I am. What’s up? · Sorry, I’m busy at seven. How about eight?
extra: Say each answer with friendly intonation.

pages.title: Group mission — plan a day together
pages.goal: Each group must agree on a plan in English: day, activity, time, place and a way to confirm.

missions.mission: Plan a Saturday afternoon. One person is busy until two: find a time that works.
Plan a dinner. The two people want different foods: agree on one place.
missions.constraint: Use “Let’s…” and “Sounds good!” at least once each.

missions.mission: Plan a study group. Find a day when everyone is free and choose a meeting place.

teach.goal: Chegar a um acordo real usando o inglês.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão.
Progressão: com apoio, palavras-chave, sem roteiro.
Peça que cada grupo anote o plano final em uma frase.
answers: Modelo: “Are you free on Saturday?” → “Yes. Let’s see a movie.” → “How about three?” → “Sounds good! I’ll text you.”
extra: What if one person says no?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short text message to invite a friend to do something this weekend.
pages.model: Hey Sam! **Are you free on** Saturday? **Let’s** see a movie. **How about** four o’clock at the mall? Let me know! **Sounds good?**
checklist: I asked if my friend is free.
I suggested a time and a place.
I closed with a question or a confirmation.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta: mensagem de convite.
solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos; mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Troquem as mensagens e respondam por escrito (Sounds good! / I’m busy).
extra: Reply with a different time.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You invited, suggested a time and a place, and confirmed the plan.
prompts.improve: Example: Stress the day and the time, not every word.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Are you free on Saturday? Let’s go to the park.
I’m busy at two. How about three, at the park gate?
ladder.goal: Change a time and a place.

ladder.say: I can’t make it on Saturday, but I’m free on Sunday if that works for you.
I’d love to join you, but I’m tied up until four; could we push it back a bit?
I’d be up for that, though I’ll have to see how the day pans out; can I confirm nearer the time?
Count me in, provisionally; I’ll let you know as soon as my schedule firms up.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
